Staged selection of interaction terms

Source: R/interaction_models.R
interaction_models.Rd

Add products of selected predictors to an L0glm model. Each stage uses the same family, constraints, weights, offsets and sparse-selection options as the main-effect fit. Products are constructed only for the selected parents, keeping the working problem small even when the original design is wide.

Arguments

interactions

Nonnegative integer controlling staged interaction generation. The default 0L fits main effects. 1L also considers pairwise products of selected main effects; 2L then considers three-way products, and so on. Each product contains distinct original predictors. Intercepts, always.include and predictor group-0 terms remain as compulsory main effects. See Details.

control.interactions

Named advanced controls: max.terms=10000L bounds the total number of generated products; max.cells=5e7 bounds rows times columns in a working design; tol=1e-8 is the relative tolerance for stopping when validation deviance worsens; and criterion=NULL chooses the information criterion used to select the final stage. A named lambda supplies that criterion; otherwise GIC is used. With l0glmTune, the tuning criterion is used, or GIC inside each CV training fit. Limits are checked before forming products.

Details

The main-effect stage first runs the requested fit, including SIS/ISIS when enabled. At stage \(d-1\), products of \(d\) currently selected original main effects are generated. Compulsory terms are retained and previously generated products remain candidates. Selection is repeated on this reduced design. Parents determine which products are considered; an interaction can remain selected after a parent main effect is discarded. Variable powers require explicitly supplied predictor columns.

For a named criterion preset, the stage penalty uses the original selectable predictor count plus the products generated so far. For example, $$\lambda_s=\log(p_0+q_s)\log\log(n)$$ for GIC, where \(p_0\) excludes compulsory terms and \(q_s\) counts generated products. Numeric lambda stays fixed across stages. Final stage scores use the common candidate count \(p_0+q_{\rm final}\) and the usual free-coefficient degrees of freedom. With predictor groups, products are grouped by the tuple of their parent group labels; named presets use coefficient-dimension group costs, as in predictor_groups. With independent validation data, its deviance selects the stage and generation stops when this deviance worsens. For quasi families with unavailable absolute likelihood criteria, stage selection uses scaled quasi-deviance plus the criterion's parameter penalty, holding the main-effect dispersion fixed. Their public likelihood criteria retain the availability reported by the supplied family.

Scalar starts retain their usual interpretation at every stage. Explicit original-coordinate vectors or matrices supply main-effect starts; new products are seeded at one in normalized coefficient coordinates, or a centered contrast for multinomial models. A product is excluded in a channel if any parent was explicitly excluded by a starting zero. Multinomial starts use row exclusions. New products have prior mean zero.

Cross-validation regenerates main-effect selection and interactions within each training fold. Prediction takes the original main-effect design and constructs the required products. Numeric and NULL starts are supported for interaction tuning. Returned path coefficients share the union of the full-data fits' generated products, with zeros for absent terms; path IC scores use this common candidate count. Fold-specific products are retained in cv$interaction_terms.

The stored training design is a lightweight view of the original matrix and product recipe. Subsetting fit$X[, j, drop=FALSE] materializes only requested columns. Dense inputs and sparse inputs retain their storage type. Preclustering uses original-channel refinement (cluster.refit=TRUE); an aggregate-only analysis can pass aggregated responses directly.

Returned recipe

fit$interactions contains order, selected_order, terms (lists of original column indices), predictor names, the fitting specification, and a history table with each stage's lambda, degrees of freedom and selection score. Sparse coefficients contain every original main effect and generated product, including excluded terms as zero. To reproduce the fitted pipeline, pass its specification together with the original X and y to do.call(l0glmFit, ...). A tuning path also includes passive zero rows from other lambda fits for display.

See also

l0glmFit, l0glmTune, predictor_groups, model_predictions

Examples

set.seed(31)
X <- matrix(rnorm(250 * 8), 250, 8)
y <- 1 + 2 * X[, 1] - 2 * X[, 2] +
  2 * X[, 1] * X[, 2] + rnorm(250)
fit <- l0glmFit(X, y, family=gaussian(), intercept=TRUE,
  lambda="gic", interactions=1L, relaxed=TRUE)
fit$interactions$history
predict(fit, X[1:5, ])
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
cv <- l0glmTune(X, y, family=gaussian(), intercept=TRUE,
  interactions=1L, tune="cv", nfolds=5L, relaxed=TRUE)
predict(cv$fit_1se, X[1:5, ])
} # }
